Good Wednesday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 534 words, a 2-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

 
 
1 big thing: Air disaster averted
 
Data: Flightradar24. Map: Will Jarrett/AP

A commercial flight from the UAE to Israel made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia today after one pilot stabbed another, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said.

  • Around 170 people were aboard the FlyDubai Boeing 737, which experienced dramatic changes in altitude and ground speed before landing. (See flight data.)

The attacking pilot was apparently trying to crash the flight before being subdued by passengers and crew, Netanyahu said — though investigators are still sorting out what happened.

  • He added that Saudi officials have arrested the suspected attacker. Their identity has not been released.
Passengers from the diverted FlyDubai flight arrive in Israel today. Photo: Jack Guez/AFP via Getty Images

FlyDubai said in a statement: "An altercation occurred in the flight deck of flight FZ 1073, operating from Dubai International (DXB) to Ben Gurion International Airport (TLV), on 30 September."

  • "The aircraft was successfully secured by on-duty flydubai crew traveling on the flight, who diverted and landed the aircraft safely at Tabuk Airport (TUU). All passengers and crew are safe and accounted for."

It remains unclear what motivated the incident, which comes amid high tensions in the Middle East and recalls a largely bygone era of hijackings — especially involving Israeli flights and passengers.

  • Get the latest.
 
 
2. 🚁 DoorDash unveils delivery drone
 
Image: DoorDash

DoorDash today unveiled a drone developed for DoorDash Air, its in-house airborne delivery service, Axios' Joann Muller reports.

  • The six-propeller drone was designed around DoorDash's own order data, including the weight and distance of typical orders.

🍕 Harrison Shih, head of DoorDash Air, tells Axios: "We didn't start with a drone and ask what would fit. We started with what people order and how local businesses actually operate, then built the entire system from there."

  • The company will begin deliveries in Northern California with restaurants including Chipotle, Popeyes and Momo N Curry.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
A U.S. Air Force C-130 Hercules prepares for takeoff from Baghdad International Airport yesterday. Photo: Ammar Karim/AFP via Getty Images
  1. 🪖 Milestone: The U.S. military announced today that it has withdrawn all American troops from Iraq, ending a 12-year mission to fight the Islamic State. President Trump posted: "Today, I am pleased to announce, that the last American Forces are leaving Iraq! It has been a long time, with very bad decision-making that got us involved in this quagmire in the first place, but soon, that will be part of History." Go deeper.
  2. 🏛️ A criminal investigation into allegations that a Cornell University student was gang-raped by seven fraternity members is fueling a new push by House Democratic women to strengthen federal protections against sexual violence on college campuses. More from Kate Santaliz.
  3. 🇬🇧 The U.K. has "strong indications" Iran played a part in the incident that saw five men arrested near a U.S.-run military air base in England, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said today. Go deeper.
 
 
4. 🖼️ 1 for the road: $450M art auction
 
Claude Monet's "Le Jardin des Tuileries" is displayed during a preview of the Blaquier-Arrieta Collection. Photo: Ben Bauer/PA via AP

A dozen Impressionist and post-Impressionist artworks valued together at almost half a billion dollars are going up for auction after sitting unseen for decades.

  • The paintings were owned by the late Argentine art collector Nelly Arrieta de Blaquier and her sugar magnate husband, Carlos Pedro Blaquier.

🎨 They include van Gogh's "Châtaigniers en fleurs" (estimated at $180 million) and Cézanne's "Arlequin" (estimated at $120 million).

  • Neither has been seen in public for half a century.
